findings.title: Significance claimed without any statistical test
findings.quote: HybridNet achieves 96.4% accuracy compared with 89.1% for the SVM, which is a significant improvement.
findings.why_it_matters: No test, p-value or interval is reported, so 'significant' is not supported; with a test set of about 154 records the difference could partly reflect chance.
findings.suggested_fix: Use repeated stratified cross-validation and a paired test (e.g. Wilcoxon signed-rank over folds) or McNemar's test on the same test predictions, and report the statistic and p-value.

findings.title: Single-run results without variability
findings.quote: The data were then split into 80% training and 20% testing sets.
findings.why_it_matters: Results come from one split and one training run; deep models vary with the random seed and split, so the reported accuracy may not be stable.
findings.suggested_fix: Repeat training over several seeds or folds and report mean ± standard deviation or 95% confidence intervals.

findings.title: Accuracy as the only metric on imbalanced data
findings.quote: The dataset is imbalanced, with 268 positive and 500 negative cases.
findings.why_it_matters: With 65% negative cases, accuracy hides how many diabetic patients are missed, which is what matters clinically.
findings.suggested_fix: Report sensitivity (recall), specificity, precision, F1 and ROC-AUC, with a confusion matrix.
